size noun

Traupman 206, 380
Traupman 206

magnitūdō, magnitūdinis f.

noun, third declension

size, bigness

Size of any kind, large or small: minōrēs sunt magnitūdine, they are smaller in size (Varro, Lewis & Short); ad fabae magnitūdinem, the size of a bean (Celsus, Lewis & Short). How big? Quantus? — Tantus! (see so big!).

Other words

  • amplitūdō, amplitūdinis f. — size, breadth, bulk

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.4.49: simulācrum modicā amplitūdine (Lewis & Short); Traupman 206, 380

    Size as extent and bulk; only in prose (Lewis & Short).

  • statūra, statūrae f. — a person’s height, build

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 2.30.4: hominēs tantulae statūrae

  • mēnsūra, mēnsūrae f. — measure; in the plural, dimensions

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Traupman 203: dimensions, mēnsūra, mēnsūrae; Ov. AA 3.265: mēnsūram facere (Lewis & Short); Traupman 304

Examples

  • hōrā ferē septimā māter mea indicat eī appārēre nūbem inūsitātā et magnitūdine et speciē.

    at about the seventh hour my mother points out to him a cloud of unusual size and appearance.Plin. Ep. 6.16.4

  • hominēs tantulae statūrae

    men of such small sizeCaes. BG 2.30.4

See also big, so big!, medium, measure.
